slot.brief: Integrate a product (e.g., log or inverse trig function times polynomial/power) using integration by parts, possibly applied twice.

verdicts.working: Integrating by parts twice gives \(\int x^2e^x\,dx=e^x(x^2-2x+2)+C\).

working:
$$\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-2\int xe^x\,dx$$
$$=x^2e^x-2(xe^x-e^x)+C=e^x(x^2-2x+2)+C$$

Independent check: Integrating by parts twice gives \(\int x^2e^x\,dx=e^x(x^2-2x+2)+C\).
solution:
Using integration by parts twice,
$$\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-2\int xe^x\,dx=e^x(x^2-2x+2)+C.$$

draft.distractor_notes:
B: Sign error in the terms produced by integration by parts.
C: Omits the final $2e^x$ contribution.
D: Fails to reduce the coefficient of $x^2$ after factoring out $e^x$.
